headline: Impeachment Day 17 Examines ₱500-Million OVP Confidential-Fund Cash Trail
seoTitle: Sara Duterte Impeachment Day 17: ₱500M OVP Funds | FMB News
seoDescription: Day 17 of Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial examined the ₱500 million OVP confidential-fund cash trail and Gina Acosta's testimony.
deck: Former OVP disbursing officer Gina Acosta testified about four ₱125-million cash releases as prosecutors questioned the handling and documentation of confidential funds.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Day 17 of Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial centered on the Office of the Vice President's ₱500 million in confidential funds and testimony from former special disbursing officer Gina Acosta.

Acosta testified that four ₱125-million cash tranches were released to Col. Raymund Dante Lachica from late 2022 through 2023. House prosecutors argued that transferring the money to an officer who was not fidelity-bonded raised accountability and compliance questions.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Acosta, called as a hostile prosecution witness, said she remained the accountable officer and described Lachica as the security officer assigned to implement confidential operations. She also confirmed that names on acknowledgment receipts were aliases and said she could not personally verify the ultimate recipients.

The defense has challenged the prosecution's interpretation of the records and emphasized liquidation documents submitted to auditors. The proceedings concern allegations under Article I of the impeachment case; testimony and prosecution arguments are not a final finding of liability against Duterte.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The testimony addresses how confidential public funds were handled, documented and accounted for, including whether liquidation paperwork sufficiently establishes who received and spent the money.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for the next prosecution witness and further testimony on the chain of custody, documentation and actual recipients of the OVP and Department of Education confidential funds.
